title: Suggestion Do the devs no longer care about MZ ? Why not update NWJS?

posts.author: jayfry
posts.body:
Do the devs not care about this engine anymore? I can't see a reason why they wouldn't update NWJS. The version that ships with the game constantly crashes on Apple Silicon.
Sure updating nwjs manually fixes it for testing, but when you try to export the game It wont run unless you put the original nwjs files back into RPGMaker resources first.
It's due to the fact that the devs Signed the resources in this game which includes the version of NWJS it shipped with. So exporting the game out with an updated version of nwjs will invalidate that signature and apple wont run it.
Or even better, don't update it, and just make nwjs optional in your signature so we can update it without apple flagging it as suspicious.

posts.author: jayfry
posts.body:
If you update NWJS manually the reason it wont work on after deploying the game for macOS because what is singed in the based game does not match what you manually put into the resources (if you update NWJS). Deploying to Web is fine, its just an issue with running the game on macOs.
A workaround is to put the packaged NWJS version back before deploying. Or buy an apple dev license and sign the whole thing yourself (which seems fine if you're gonna release the game anyways)
I wouldn't have an issue if the current packaged version of NWJS didn't crash all the time with apple silicon. It never crashes when updating NWJS to the latest version. This is why I ask if they even care about the game anymore
They should at least update to fix this, or give us other options

old or new
version of nw.js,
ALL outputted games for MacOS will flag as dangerous on every mac that downloads it

The only fix for this that I know of, is to enroll as an apple developer.

This is nearly identical to the unorthodox
update instructions
; it usually works. It only stopped working for me until recently, when I updated it within the last few months. Many people are encountering these issues like this even on different engines.
C# with Monogame was an option, but it doesn't quite have the wide-spread support that I wanted for my solution. Then RPG Maker Unite would be a possibility.
I considered using an RPG Maker export to a progressive web app (PWA) with Universal Windows Platform (UWP). Then I throw that into a Javascript wrapper (great, but a lot of massaging). This option was also not a good long-term solution.
I looked at a transpiler from Javascript to C++, but that could make devs cry.
As far as I can see, staying with RPG Maker MZ at the most compatible and stable version seems to be the best bet. I'm working on a long porting guide to go with this process. If you know any other options for porting, please chime in.
In regard to solving the OP's issue, I'm uncertain how exactly NWJS would crash easily when it was the most stable and compatible. It isn't too different than running Chrome and Node by itself. I'm curious if there are plugins or memory issues that are the root cause? I just got off Messenger with a friend and his Mac. He is having issues with his RAM sticks. If the manufacturing time and usage was similar, it could be a possibility for you too. Apple usually manufactures in batches.
Could you run Chrome debugger tool (It was Command+Option+J) and see if anything pops up prior to a crash or check?
Alternatively, you can check the Console app (You’ll also find it at Finder > Applications > Utilities > Console. The Console app, also known as Console.app, is like a Windows Event Viewer for Mac).
Do you see any correlating messages to determine the root cause?
